newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says oil futures listing is up to industry.
newsitem.headline: Japan says oil futures listing is up to industry.

text.p: Japan said on Monday it will not endorse the listing of oil futures contracts in Tokyo unless the domestic oil industry supports the idea.

"It's unrealistic to carry this (the listing of oil futures) out as long as the (oil) industry finds it (the oil futures contract) unnecessary," said an official at the Ministry of International Trade and Industry's (MITI) agency of natural resources and energy, which oversees Japan's energy industry.
"It's the oil firms trading physical cargoes on a daily basis, not speculators, that should play the central role in futures markets," the official said.
Kyodo news agency reported on Saturday that the government had drafted a report saying an oil futures market could become an effective means of setting fair market prices in Japan.
The official said he was not aware of any new official government report on the subject, adding that Kyodo may have been referring to a report by one of its study panels.
The agency's February report on the U.S. oil market pointed to the New York Mercantile Exchange's (NYMEX) positive role in price formation, but did not mention its implications for Japan.
The Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) has been studying the possibility of listing oil products and crude oil futures from as early as fiscal 1998/1999, which starts April 1, 1998.
But the Petroleum Association of Japan (PAJ), an industry group made up of oil refiners and wholesalers, has maintained a cautious attitude toward the introduction of oil futures.

"We have no intention to deny (the value) of futures markets themselves," a PAJ spokesman said on Monday. "But we believe the need for oil futures among oil companies here is not yet high enough to introduce them," he said.
The MITI energy agency official said the government will continue to study the listing of oil futures as one of several options to make the process of domestic oil price formation more transparent.
